title: Quantum Decision Studio
subtitle: Constrained allocation and variational correlated-electron research.

cases.label: Constrained allocation
cases.title: Optimize the allocation. Keep the constraints.
cases.description: Eight synthetic assets, exactly three holdings, turnover costs and correlated risk. Compare a number-preserving quantum ansatz with exhaustive enumeration and classical local search.

charts.title: Sensitivity to an explicit uniform-output mixture

method: Objective = 4 wᵀΣw − μᵀw + 0.003‖w−w_previous‖₁; equal weights on exactly three of eight assets. Covariance is positive definite by construction.

Depth-2 cost phases alternate with an exact ring-XY mixer in the 56-state feasible sector. Six seeded Nelder–Mead restarts each have a 350-iteration cap. Uniform feasible-state preparation is assumed, not compiled.
Exact enumeration gives A, D, H. Swap local search gives A, D, H, cost -0.038294, after 30 neighbour evaluations. The ansatz is not claimed to outperform either baseline.
limitations: Synthetic forward-looking means/covariance: no historical backtest or investment claim. Small exact simulation is the reference, not evidence of scalability.
Mixer construction and dense exponentiation operate in a constrained subspace; physical preparation, compiled gates and measurement overhead are not benchmarked.
Uniform probability mixing is a sensitivity model, not calibrated gate noise. Both expected objective and success probability must be inspected.

cases.label: Correlated electrons
cases.title: Follow electrons from hopping to localization.
cases.description: A spinful two-site Hubbard dimer isolates the competition between electron hopping and on-site repulsion. A symmetry-preserving variational state is checked against exact and analytic ground-state energies.
method: Construct −t Σσ(c†₀σc₁σ+h.c.) + UΣᵢnᵢ↑nᵢ↓ using fermionic parity signs; restrict to one spin-up and one spin-down electron.
Three real two-level Givens rotations span the four-state real sector. Three seeded BFGS starts minimize the statevector energy for each interaction.
Each result obeys the variational bound and agrees with E₀=(U−√(U²+16t²))/2 within 10⁻⁶ t. Double occupancy is a separate observable, not inferred from a fitted curve.
limitations: This is an effective correlated-electron benchmark, not an ab initio molecule or a battery-material prediction. It is a foundation for extending the battery-design theme.
The ansatz can span this tiny real sector; success does not demonstrate a scalable chemistry algorithm.
Finite-shot evaluation is shown in the Hubbard measurements case. Molecular geometry, basis-set error, device noise and battery voltage are not represented.

cases.label: Hubbard measurements
cases.title: Can sampled observables resolve electron localization?
cases.description: Measure energy, total double occupancy and kinetic energy of the optimized dimer state. Choose a shot budget and compare grouped measurements with independent Pauli measurements at the same total preparations. Confidence intervals refer to prepared-state expectations; the table exports both strategies at all budgets.
method: Independent Born multinomial draws after local Pauli basis rotations; exact-expectation VQE training
Two-sided Hoeffding per active group, union bound within each observable; marginal 95% CIs for prepared-state expectations
Orbital order: 0-up, 0-down, 1-up, 1-down (orbital 0 is least significant bit). Hopping = −(XZXI+YZYI+IXZX+IYZY)/2. D = (2I−ZIII−IZII−IIZI−IIIZ+ZZII+IIZZ)/4. Energy = kinetic + U D, with t=1.
One ZZZZ shot evaluates all density terms together, retaining covariance. Four additional local settings measure hopping parities. Raw 16-outcome counts and seeds are included in results/latest.json.

Equal shots within each strategy; five grouped settings at n shots versus ten independent Pauli terms at n/2 shots, matching total preparations. All observables share those counts. Identity costs no shots. Counts exclude exact training, state preparation and gate compilation. Neither allocation is optimized.

Ungrouped density uses six independent Pauli means plus the exact identity offset 1/2. Confidence bounds use each coefficient times its measurement range. Exact sampling SD is computed from Born probabilities as a diagnostic; sample SE is estimated from counts. Neither is the confidence-bound half-width.
limitations: Ideal CPU simulation of independent Born shots; no device noise or finite-shot optimization. The exact trained state is held fixed during measurement.

Intervals cover prepared-state expectations, not ansatz bias. They are conservative, marginal per observable, and not simultaneous across the scan. Sample SE is descriptive, not the CI formula; bounds can extend outside physical ranges.

A small fully expressive Hubbard dimer with t=1; no materials prediction or quantum advantage. Matched preparations exclude circuit and basis-switching costs. Equal shots per setting are not optimized for either strategy.
